newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli says impact of Iranian revolution waning.
newsitem.headline: Israeli says impact of Iranian revolution waning.

text.p: Israel's chief policy-maker for Lebanon said on Sunday the election results in arch-foe Iran showed the force of the Islamic revolution was waning.

Although Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it was too early to draw conclusions, Uri Lubrani told Israel's army radio he was pleased by the landslide victory by moderate candidate Mohammad Khatami in Iranian elections.
"I feel a certain relief," said the policy chief for Lebanon, where Israeli forces are battling Iranian-backed guerrillas.
"The force of the influence of Khomeini's revolution is waning. This is a clear affront mainly by the young people and the women against this regime," he said.

However, Lubrani said: "We must not forget that the person who makes the decisions in Iran -- unless this changes as well, and I don't see a change at this moment -- is still (supreme leader Ayatollah Ali) Khamenei."
Netanyahu, speaking to reporters at his office, said he hoped the development was positive but thought it was "too early to assess what is happening in Iran."

Khatami, 54, a senior clergyman's son and a former culture and Islamic guidance minister, is considered an open-minded religious intellectual and tolerant politician. He advocates more personal freedom, democracy and the rule of law.

Khatami crushed conservative parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri who had been backed by the religious establishment that has ruled Iran since fundamentalist clerics toppled the pro-American Shah in 1979.
Commercial and military ties between Israel and Iran gave way to belligerence after the 1979 revolution.
Israel accuses Tehran of arming Hizbollah (Party of God) militants who are waging a guerrilla war to oust Israeli troops from a 15 km (nine-mile) wide south Lebanon occupation zone.
Israel also says Iran is responsible for the fate of its missing airman Ron Arad whose bomber was shot down over Lebanon in 1986. Tehran denies knowledge of his whereabouts.
